panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is an H&E view of the tumor showing the architectural growth pattern consistent with VIPoma. B: Panel B shows high-power H&E detail demonstrating the characteristic cytomorphology of VIPoma, specifically the salt-and-pepper chromatin. C: Panel C demonstrates strong positive immunoreactivity for the neuroendocrine marker CD56, supporting the diagnosis of VIPoma. D: Panel D shows Ki-67 staining highlighting only a small fraction of neoplastic cells (2%), classifying the tumor as low-grade.
panels.attribution_text: Dahmani et al. Recurrent primary hepatic VIPoma treated with a combination of surgical resection and loco-regional therapy.. Future science OA 2023. doi:10.2144/fsoa-2022-0046. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Histological features of the hepatic VIPoma. (A) Glandular architecture of the tumor (Hematoxylin-eosin x100). (B) Tumor cells are monotonous and display round nuclei and moderate amounts of eosinophilic cytoplasm. Nuclei show a characteristic stippled (“salt and pepper”) chromatin pattern with inconspicuous nucleoli (Hematoxylin-eosin x400). (C) The tumor is diffusely and strongly positive for CD56 immunostaining (×400). (D) The proliferation marker Ki-67 highlights 2% of the neoplastic cells (arrow), consistent with a low proliferation index (×400).
in_text_mentions: onotonous with “salt and pepper” nuclear chromatin. Immunohistochemical staining revealed that tumor cells were diffusely positive for neuroendocrine markers (synaptophysin, chromogranin A and CD56) (Figure 3). Anti-VIP antibodies were not however available. Based on the pathological findings and the serum VIP level, we concluded to a recurrence of hepatic VIPoma. A mitotic count of 1 per 10 high power fields, and Ki-67 index estimated at 2%, categorized the tumor as a low-grade one. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: CT axial section of the liver showing spontaneously hypodense lesions, consistent with the presentation of a VIPoma. B: CT axial section of the liver during the arterial phase, showing intense enhancement of hepatic lesions, consistent with hypervascular VIPoma. C: CT axial section of the liver during the portal phase, showing washout of contrast product from hepatic lesions, characteristic of hypervascular VIPoma.

The lesions were spontaneously hypodense, intensely enhancing after injection of contrast product in the arterial phase with a wash out in the portal phase (Figure 1). The lesions were hyperintense on T2- and diffusion weighted MRI, enhancing in the arterial phase with a wash out in the portal and late phases (Figure 2). Octreotide scan failed to visualize any hepatic lesion. Ultrasound-guided liver biopsy of the lesions was performed revealing a tumor cell proliferation with glandular architecture.
